summary: The trend backdrop is healthy (SPY 6.89% above its 200-day, 20-day realized vol only 8.85%), but leadership is rotating away from tech and small caps while credit and bonds are soft. Keep normal appetite with a bias to defensive and broad-breadth exposure rather than adding aggressively to growth.
reasons: Regime is on: SPY closed 773.09 vs 200-day SMA 723.23, 6.89% above; 63-day return +4.99%, but 21-day return is flat at -0.04%, so the advance has stalled.
Volatility is calm: SPY 20-day realized vol 8.85% vs 12.67% over 252 days; VIXY 21-day +1.03% and 63-day -23.55%, so no fear spike.
Breadth is improving under a flat index: RSP (equal weight) 5-day +2.15% and 21-day +1.80% vs SPY 21-day -0.04%.
Growth is the weak spot: QQQ 21-day -2.98%, XLK -3.94%, XLC -4.02% (XLC is 3.39% below its 200-day); XLK 5-day -0.99% and QQQ 5-day -0.51% show it is not yet turning.
Small caps are mixed: IWM 5-day +1.88% but 21-day -3.74%, 63-day -5.10%, and sitting at its 200-day (-0.17%).
Credit is softening: HYG 21-day -1.71% and 1.18% below its 200-day; LQD 21-day -1.37%, 2.58% below its 200-day. Not a stress signal, but it does not confirm risk-on.
Long yields have been rising over the month: TLT 21-day -1.45% (3.72% below its 200-day), IEF 21-day -0.68%, though TLT bounced 5-day +1.71%, so yields eased this week.
Gold is weak: GLD 21-day -5.28% and 8.61% below its 200-day, with a firmer dollar (UUP 21-day +1.54%, 3.79% above its 200-day) over the month; the dollar eased 5-day -0.69%.
Sector leadership is defensive plus energy: XLE 21-day +10.33% (63-day +15.47%), XLV +5.33%, XLP +5.29%; cyclicals XLI (21-day -1.15%, 63-day -7.24%) and XLRE (63-day -5.65%) lag.

asset_class_view.equity_etfs: Broad US is fine: VOO 21-day -0.03%, 6.93% above its 200-day, vol 12.6%. Prefer VOO/VTI over QQQ (21-day -2.98%, vol 19.8%). International is weaker: VXUS 21-day -3.99%, VWO -4.78% and sitting on its 200-day (+0.02%), so not attractive. VNQ is risky: 63-day -6.49%, 1.66% below its 200-day.
asset_class_view.bonds_gold: Unattractive for now: BND 63-day -1.04% and 1.52% below its 200-day; IEF 63-day -1.80%; TLT 63-day -2.37% and the most rate-sensitive (vol 9.4%). Gold (GLD) fell 5.28% in 21 days and is 8.61% below its 200-day with 29.3% vol, so it is a falling knife rather than a hedge. Only short Treasuries (SHY, 21-day +0.26%) are holding value.
asset_class_view.crypto: Constructive but volatile: BTC 63-day +21.2%, 15.5% above its 200-day, 21-day +0.55%, vol 44%. ETH is weaker (21-day -7.93%, vol 61%) though still 14.8% above its 200-day. If used, size BTC small and ETH smaller.

watch: SPY closing below its 200-day SMA (723.23) would turn the regime filter off and flip the stance to risk-off.

Tech/growth stabilizing: QQQ and XLK 5-day returns turning positive would move the stance toward risk-on; a further drop in QQQ (21-day already -2.98%) toward its 200-day (+7.39% away) would lean risk-off.
Credit: HYG falling through its 200-day further or a 21-day drop beyond about -3% would signal stress.
A VIXY jump after the recent quiet (5-day +0.73%) or SPY realized vol rising well above its 12.7% yearly average.
Long yields: TLT making a new low (80.24 now, 3.72% below its 200-day) would pressure equities and REITs.
